passages.title: Remembered faith and personal support answer shame about a chained teacher
passages.summary: The letter is addressed from Paul to Timothy, his beloved child. Paul remembers Timothy’s tears and longs to see him. He recalls the faith of Timothy’s grandmother Lois and mother Eunice. Timothy is to stir up God’s gift, given through Paul’s hands. God gave a spirit of power, love, and self-control, not fear. Timothy should not be ashamed of the Lord or of Paul the prisoner. All in Asia turned away from Paul. Onesiphorus was not ashamed of his chain and searched for him in Rome.
passages.uncertainty: No exact location is assigned to unnamed or heavenly settings.

lds.text: The selected Church lesson teaches courage through power, love, and a sound mind. How does remembered family faith support courage before present danger?

contextNote.title: Remembered faith and personal support answer shame about a chained teacher
contextNote.text: Paul writes as a prisoner (verse 8), and many have left him (verse 15). Shame is the danger the chapter names three times. Verse 8 tells Timothy not to be ashamed of the Lord’s testimony or of Paul. Verse 12 says Paul is not ashamed, for he knows whom he trusted. Verse 16 praises Onesiphorus, who was not ashamed of the chain. The ground for courage comes just before, in verse 7. God gave a spirit of power, love, and self-control.

passages.title: Patient correction must accompany careful teaching and shared endurance
passages.summary: Timothy is to be strong in grace and pass the teaching to faithful people. He should endure hardship like a soldier, an athlete, and a farmer. Paul suffers in chains, but God’s word is not chained. A trustworthy saying follows: if we died with him, we will live with him. Timothy should avoid word fights and empty talk. Hymenaeus and Philetus say the resurrection has already happened. A great house has vessels for honor and for dishonor. The Lord’s servant must be gentle and correct opponents with patience.
passages.uncertainty: No exact location is assigned to unnamed or heavenly settings.

lds.text: Why must correction remain gentle when false teaching harms others?

contextNote.title: Patient correction must accompany careful teaching and shared endurance
contextNote.text: Verse 23 tells Timothy to refuse foolish questions, because they breed quarrels. Verse 24 gives the rule for the Lord’s servant: he must not quarrel. Three qualities replace quarreling: gentle toward all, able to teach, and patient. Verse 25 keeps correction in place but sets its tone: gentleness. The reason is hope for the opponent. God may give them repentance and knowledge of the truth. Verse 26 says they may yet escape the devil’s snare.

passages.title: Received Scripture equips conduct amid deceptive displays of religion
passages.summary: The letter warns that hard times will come in the last days. People will love themselves, money, and pleasure more than God. They will hold a form of godliness and deny its power. Such teachers resist the truth as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses. Timothy has followed Paul’s teaching, conduct, and sufferings at Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra. All who live godly lives in Christ will be persecuted. Timothy should continue in what he learned from childhood in the holy Scriptures. Every Scripture is God-breathed and useful.
passages.uncertainty: No exact location is assigned to unnamed or heavenly settings.

lds.text: The selected Church lesson teaches that Scripture can make readers wise for salvation. How does Scripture's usefulness lead into good work rather than knowledge alone?

contextNote.title: Received Scripture equips conduct amid deceptive displays of religion
contextNote.text: Verse 13 says deceivers will grow worse. Verse 14 tells Timothy to stay with what he has learned. Verse 15 says the holy Scriptures can make him wise for salvation. Verse 16 lists four uses: teaching, reproof, correction, and training in righteousness. Verse 17 gives the purpose of all four. The person who belongs to God becomes complete. He is equipped “for every good work,” so the end of the list is action.

passages.title: Urgent teaching and ordinary needs stand together near the speaker's expected departure
passages.summary: Paul charges Timothy before God and Christ, the judge of living and dead. Timothy is to announce the word and be ready at all times. A time will come when people gather teachers who please their ears. Paul says he is already being poured out. He has fought the good fight and kept the faith. He asks Timothy to come soon and bring Mark, a cloak, and the books. At his first defense no one stood with him, but the Lord did. He sends greetings and a blessing.
passages.uncertainty: No exact location is assigned to unnamed or heavenly settings.

lds.text: The selected Church lesson teaches continued faithfulness when hearers prefer false teaching. Why do ordinary requests remain beside confident language about completion and reward?

contextNote.title: Urgent teaching and ordinary needs stand together near the speaker's expected departure
contextNote.text: Verse 1 sets the charge before God and Christ the judge. Verse 2 gives five commands in a row. The first is to announce the word. The second is to be ready in season and out of season. Reprove, rebuke, and exhort follow, with patience and teaching. Verses 3–4 explain the urgency: hearers will turn from the truth to fables. Verse 6 adds another reason: Paul’s own departure is near.
